It's important to note that this data is probably not representing a hidden kill-switch type slow down happening to devices when they reach a certain age, what happens typically is that a new Operating System version is released around the same time as the new phones. Loading this newer operating system on an older iPhone results in slower performance.

You could argue that this is intentional and that Apple is trying to slow down the older models by intentionally making their new operating system run slower, but it seems to me it is equally likely that the newer operating system built specifically for newer models just runs slower on older iPhones. Some people want a specific feature in the new O/S software, so they do the upgrade, without realizing that while their older iPhone can run it, it is naturally not going to run as fast.

It’s important to keep in mind that, although Apple could be purposefully slowing down older models in order to convince you to purchase their newer ones, this is not a hard fact. Smartphones and laptops naturally slow down over time, especially when you’re updating your software and apps constantly as well as filling them steadily with more digital debris.
